fields.expected: Yes. Most of my work has been building software and machine-learning systems against real healthcare and operations data. At Intelehealth I worked on AI and data systems for rural telemedicine, including a Python resource-availability scoring pipeline across 32 villages that combined facility-tier classification, geospatial distance, Google Maps data, weather, and healthcare-resource availability, plus an evaluation framework comparing AI-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case clinical standard using stratified sampling to surface systematic failure modes. Currently I build the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system at Summer Atlantic Capital, where I own the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI microservice, the detection API, and a learning-to-rank layer, because an anomaly system that floods analysts with alerts just creates a second problem. I also served as lead model developer on a Gates Foundation-funded Hopkins project, training XGBoost models on roughly 10 million survey records with SHAP-based interpretation. I am comfortable in Python and TypeScript, and I care most about whether a system holds up against messy real data rather than a clean demo.
